rationale.conceptual: The method combines a standard kMC framework with a custom energetic-deposition probability formula (explicitly given) and a barrier model (Breeman et al.) using an EAM potential and Newton-Raphson saddle-point search. This is a multi-part documented algorithm that needs understanding of atomistic simulation, but no novel theoretical derivation.
rationale.execution: The workflow is a 2-3 stage pipeline: simulation, island analysis, and Bragg/roughness analysis. All stages can be implemented in a single script using standard Python libraries, with straightforward I/O and a single external data file.

difficulty.reasoning: Implementing a kinetic Monte Carlo simulator with a custom deposition rule and EAM-based barrier calculations requires careful implementation of several non-trivial components, but all are drawn from published methods. The pipeline is simple, with only two scored analysis outputs derived from a single simulation run, and no complex tooling.

compute_estimate.reasoning: Kinetic Monte Carlo on a 160x160x4 lattice up to 5 ML is CPU-bound and trivially small; memory footprint is low, and the only input is a tiny EAM potential file.
